# Gelabber v0.8.0

Integrated through the PRs #321-#347, #351, #357, #358, #360-#373 into `v0.8`
and the version PR into `main`.

**Operators: read "Upgrade notes" first.** Three database migrations run on
the first start (no rollback without a backup). Take the new `compose.yaml`,
`Caddyfile` and `.env.example` from this checkout and recreate the proxy.
Without a public MinIO host, set `ATTACHMENT_DELIVERY=proxy`. Clients older
than v0.8 can no longer go live.

## New look and feel

The web app and the desktop app got a full design and UX overhaul (#322-#330).

- **Themes and controls** (#322). Account themes reach every surface,
  including the light themes; links, mentions and focus rings stay readable
  in all 14 built-in themes, and fields have a visible border. Dialogs have a
  fixed header with "Schließen" and become bottom sheets on phones; a dialog
  with unsaved changes asks before it closes. Toasts are themed cards with an
  optional "Rückgängig" and pause while hovered. Cold start shows the logo
  instead of a blank page.
- **First run and invites** (#323). Sign-in, registration and invite pages
  share one layout. An invite opened while signed out leads through
  registration and back to the invite. A new account is greeted with
  "Server erstellen" or "Einladung einfügen"; the "+" in the server rail does
  both and accepts full links, links without scheme and bare codes, so the
  desktop app and the installed PWA can join servers. A new server opens with
  a ready-to-copy invite and starts with a voice room "Wohnzimmer". Sign-in
  says when a session ended, shows a password toggle and a Caps Lock hint, and
  retries on its own when the server does not answer.
- **Finding your way** (#324). The top bar on phones names the place and
  shows unread and mention counts; the drawer opens with an edge swipe and is
  part of the Back history. The rail returns to the last channel of a server,
  and Strg+K opens a quick switcher.
- **Chat** (#325). A channel with unread messages opens at the first unread
  one under "N neue Nachrichten seit HH:MM" with "Springen" and "Als gelesen
  markieren (Esc)"; nothing is marked read before you reach the end. Failed
  sends stay in place with "Erneut senden", and message actions live in one
  menu (long press on phones).
- **Call bar** (#326). The call bar sits at the bottom of the window at every
  width and shows the real call state: connecting, connection quality with
  latency and loss, reconnecting. The joined voice channel shows a green
  speaker in the channel list (#330).
- **Voice room** (#327). One line says who is there; Lives sit on a stage
  with a spotlight and a filmstrip; each person has one card, with volume and
  profile behind "…". Fullscreen has a control strip that hides when idle.
  The gear opens quick settings (devices, send level, volumes, voice mode).
- **Settings** (#328) open inside the workspace (`/settings/…`) with areas
  for account and app; Darstellung offers light/dark/system and a text size,
  themes preview across the app before you keep them, and the profile card
  editor keeps its preview in view. Server settings show invite uses and
  expiry, ask before revoking a link, and move kick/ban into a "…" menu.
- **Motion and details** (#329). Short, quiet animations for dialogs, sheets,
  popovers, toasts, drawers and the call bar; a live message fades in, your
  own one brightens once the server confirms it, and copy buttons say
  "Kopiert". "Bewegung reduzieren" (or the system setting) turns all of it
  off.
- Toasts no longer cover the newest message's actions: the list makes room
  above the composer (#368).
- Voice room and settings load as their own chunks after start, which cuts
  the initial JavaScript from 977 to 893 kB (#361). After a reconnect only the
  conversations on screen reload their history, spread over a second (#332).

## Calls

- **One "Live gehen"** (#330, #353). Screen sharing and Go Live are one
  feature: "Live gehen" shares a screen (with its sound where the platform
  allows it), several people can be live at once, and viewers watch inside
  the voice channel with "Zuschauen". The sidebar, the member list and a hint
  in the text channel show who is live. The `go_live` permission is now
  labelled "Live gehen" and gates screen sharing; members have it by default.
  The single per-channel Live claim, its `l`/`la` tracks, the `lc` nonce and
  the watch-only join were removed from the API, the media gateway and the
  app (#353).
- The media server refuses a screen or its sound from a ticket without the
  Live permission (#352, #373). Someone who was granted it during a call is
  asked to rejoin the voice channel to go live (#367).
- **Louder playback** (#357). Conversation, stream and per-user volume go up
  to 400 %; the sliders keep 100 % in the middle.
- **Hardware AV1** (#347). Video uses AV1 where the device encodes it in
  hardware and every receiver in the room decodes it in hardware, then H.264
  in hardware, else VP8. The desktop app encodes and decodes AV1 on the GPU
  (NVIDIA, Intel, AMD through GStreamer on Linux; Media Foundation on Windows)
  and falls back to software AV1 if the hardware encoder fails mid-call.
- **Media workers** (#337). `MEDIA_WORKERS` runs several mediasoup workers,
  one CPU core and one UDP port each (10000 up to `MEDIA_ICE_PORT_MAX`). A
  new voice channel goes to the least busy worker. A worker that dies closes
  only its own channels, whose clients rejoin, and is restarted on the same
  port. See "Media workers" in `deploy/README.md`.
- **Limits for the media WebSocket** (#334). Each client address may hold 16
  `/media/ws` sockets that have not joined a call yet (`MEDIA_PENDING_PER_IP`),
  the SFU 1024 in total (`MEDIA_PENDING_MAX`); past either cap the upgrade is
  answered `429` or `503`. A joined socket is pinged every 20 s
  (`MEDIA_HEARTBEAT_MS`) and leaves the call after 60 s without any answer
  (`MEDIA_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS`), so a peer whose connection died without a close
  no longer stays in the room. The app rejoins on its own once the connection
  is back.
- Media checks a peer's authority once per attach pass and creates consumers
  in parallel with a bound, so a large room fills faster (#333).

## Chat

- **No more double messages** (#355, #369). Your own message no longer shows
  twice for a moment when its live event arrives before the send answer.
- **System messages** (#336). "X ist live in Y." is now a system message:
  it cannot be edited, shows correctly in replies, and its push text comes
  from one catalog on the server.
- **Link previews say why a link got no card** (#349, #371). The API log has
  one `info` line per link without a card, with its host and a reason
  (`refused`, `dns`, `timeout`, `status`, `content_type`, `no_metadata`, …),
  and `/metrics` counts them in `gelabber_link_previews_total` and
  `gelabber_link_preview_images_total`. A card whose image cannot be stored
  keeps its text. TikTok links get a card with title and image: the preview
  agent now ends in `like Twitterbot`. Hosts that resolve to a LAN address
  still get no card, on purpose; see "Link previews" in `deploy/README.md`.
- **Faster GIF search, fewer KLIPY requests** (#350, #370). Search and
  trending pages are kept in Redis for 10 minutes and shared by all users
  (`KLIPY_CACHE_SECS`, `0` turns it off), so a repeated search answers at
  once and costs no request from the key's quota. When KLIPY answers 429 the
  API stops asking it for the `Retry-After` (60 s by default) and the picker
  says the server's GIF quota is used up and when to try again, instead of
  loading. `/metrics` adds `gelabber_upstream_request_duration_seconds` for
  KLIPY's response times and `gelabber_cache_total` for cache hits. KLIPY
  testing keys allow only 100 requests per hour for the whole instance; see
  "GIFs" in `deploy/README.md`.
- Unread counts and "mark as read" no longer walk the whole history of a
  channel with nothing new since you joined (#340): on a large test database
  `UNREAD` went from about 1 s to 6 ms.

## Attachments

- **Attachments through the API** (#348, #372). With
  `ATTACHMENT_DELIVERY=proxy` browsers upload and load attachments on the
  app's own origin and the API streams them to and from MinIO, so MinIO needs
  no public host, port or CORS setting. The default, `redirect`, keeps
  presigned MinIO links as before. Video seeking works in both. See
  "Attachments through the API" in `deploy/README.md`.
- **Broken pictures say so** (#348). A picture that cannot load shows
  "Bild konnte nicht geladen werden." with a retry and a download link
  instead of an empty grey box.
- **Startup warnings for `MINIO_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT`** (#348). Behind TLS
  (`API_COOKIE_SECURE=true`) the API warns when the endpoint is a loopback
  address or plain HTTP; as before, it warns about an `https://` port other
  than 443.

## Notifications

- **Desktop app: native notifications** (#339). New messages arrive as the
  system's own notifications (Windows toasts; the notification service on
  Linux: mako, KDE, GNOME, dunst) while the window is not in front. Clicking
  one opens the conversation. Mute and "Inhalt in Benachrichtigungen
  verbergen" apply as before. **Changed default:** in the desktop app these
  notifications are on unless they were switched off before (Einstellungen →
  Benachrichtigungen). Uninstalling on Windows removes the app's notification
  registration.
- **Deleted messages recall their push** (#340). Deleting a message within
  an hour of its push quietly replaces its notification with "Nachricht
  gelöscht", and a push still queued at the push service is dropped. On
  Safari/iOS the quiet notice also shows when the notification was already
  swiped away.

## Security

- **Sliding sessions** (#341, #195). A sign-in lasts at most 30 days
  (`API_SESSION_TTL_HOURS`, default `720`) and ends earlier after 14 days
  without use (`API_SESSION_IDLE_HOURS`, default `336`). Any use extends the
  idle window; an open Gelabber tab or app counts as use. A device that stays
  away longer signs in again, and its push notifications stop with its
  session.
- **Stricter Content-Security-Policy** (#342, #288). Once the web container
  knows `MINIO_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT`, the policy also limits where the app may
  load images, media and connections from. Without the variable it keeps the
  v0.7.1 policy and logs that. See "Content-Security-Policy" in
  `deploy/README.md`.
- Rate limits for signed-in requests count per account, not per address, and
  are resolved once per request (#338, #287).
- Deleting a server or cutting voice permissions revokes all members in one
  Redis round trip, and message, reaction and DM writes hand their realtime
  event to a background worker instead of publishing it before answering
  (#344, #294).
- Revocations (kick, ban, leave, server or channel delete, session revoke)
  reach open sockets on another API process at once through a Redis notice
  (#346, #293).

## Fixes and performance

- Gateway load no longer grows with sockets × servers: voice rosters are read
  once per server, and sockets without a voice seat check the database every
  10 s instead of every second (#346).
- Internal: large modules split without behaviour changes (`media/src/sfu/`,
  the desktop media core, the gateway hub, the voice session and the message
  pane; #331, #335, #343, #345, #360, #362, #363, #365).

## Build

- Leaner CI workflows; CI now also runs on pushes to version branches (#351).

## Upgrade notes

- **Back up first** (`deploy/backup.sh`) or pause Watchtower: migrations
  0025 (`push_receipts` and an index on messages; message writes wait while
  the index builds), 0026 (`messages.system_kind` and
  `system_params`) and 0027 (session idle window) run on start. 0027 caps
  existing sessions at 14 days from the upgrade.

- **Update the checkout and recreate the proxy.** Watchtower swaps only the
  images, so bring the server checkout to the release for the new
  `compose.yaml`, `Caddyfile` and `.env.example` (`git pull`, or
  `git fetch --tags && git checkout v0.8.0`), then run `docker compose up -d`
  and `docker compose up -d --no-deps --force-recreate proxy`. The new
  `compose.yaml` hands `MINIO_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT` to `web` (CSP) and
  `ATTACHMENT_DELIVERY` to `api` and `web`; the new `Caddyfile` hands media
  the client address. Without the new `compose.yaml` the web container keeps
  the v0.7.1 CSP and the proxy mode does not work.

- **Check `MINIO_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT`** (#348). With the default
  `ATTACHMENT_DELIVERY=redirect` every browser must reach it: its own host on
  443 behind your proxy (`deploy/README.md`, "MinIO on 443"), not
  `localhost` and not a port such as `:9000` that is closed from outside.
  Look for warnings about it in the API log after the upgrade. Without a
  second domain, set `ATTACHMENT_DELIVERY=proxy` in `.env` and run
  `docker compose up -d api web` (needs the v0.8 `compose.yaml`, which hands
  the setting to both containers); a proxy in front must then allow 25 MiB
  request bodies on `/api`. Set `MINIO_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT` in `.env`, not in
  the `api` service, and recreate `web` together with `api` after changing
  it (#342).

- **Clients older than v0.8 lose Go Live** (#353). Their Go Live button now
  fails: the server answers the old `l`/`la` track and the watch-only join with
  `bad_request`. Voice, camera and screen sharing keep working. Update the
  desktop app and reload the web app to go live again. Old `gb:live:*` keys in
  Redis expire on their own. A browser tab left open across the update shows
  new live notices as an empty row until it is reloaded (#336).

- **Media workers** (#337): with `MEDIA_WORKERS` above 1, set
  `MEDIA_ICE_PORT_MAX` to at least `10000 + MEDIA_WORKERS - 1` (media refuses
  to start otherwise) and open and forward the whole UDP range on the host
  firewall and the router. A missing port breaks voice only for the channels
  on that worker. The default stays one worker on UDP 10000.

- **Own Caddy in front (homelab overlay):** add
  `header_up X-Forwarded-For {client_ip}` to the media upstream, as in
  `deploy/compose/Caddyfile.homelab`, and reload Caddy. The bundled Caddy
  gets it with the new `Caddyfile` (recreate the `proxy` container, see
  "Rollout and rollback with exact digests" in `deploy/README.md`). Media
  counts its pending-socket cap by the rightmost `X-Forwarded-For` entry.
  Without the line, clients behind a CDN or tunnel your Caddy trusts all
  count as that proxy and share its 16 slots, so after a server restart many
  reconnects get `429` and are retried. A proxy other than Caddy must send
  the client address in `X-Forwarded-For` (Nginx:
  `$proxy_add_x_forwarded_for`). Media logs a warning when its cap refuses a
  private address that sent no such header.
- **Keep `GELABBER_MEDIA_BIND` on loopback** (homelab overlay): like the API,
  media believes `X-Forwarded-For` from whoever reaches its port.

- **Sessions:** if you set `API_SESSION_IDLE_HOURS`, keep it at most
  `API_SESSION_TTL_HOURS`; the API refuses to start otherwise.

- **Desktop, Linux (Arch):** for AV1 on the GPU, `gst-plugins-bad` (with
  `av1parse`, NVIDIA through nvcodec) and `gst-plugin-va` (Intel/AMD) are
  needed, the same optional packages as for H.264. The PKGBUILD's optdepends
  and `desktop/README.md` say so.
- **Desktop, Windows:** the installer and `latest.json` are attached to this
  release; 0.7.x apps offer the update.

## Open

- Not tested on physical devices: hardware AV1 encoding and decoding
  (NVIDIA RTX 40, Intel Arc, AMD RX 7000, Windows MF) and the fallback when a
  receiver lacks it; native notifications on Windows, KDE, GNOME and
  Hyprland; the redesign on a real iPhone and Android phone; several media
  workers under load. The strict CSP still needs a manual check in Firefox
  and Safari.
- Open issues: #165 (desktop tracker), #356 (a second language for system
  messages and pushes).
